title: Govardhan lifted

segments.voice: Yesterday, Govardhan lifted began with a question: the village turned its offering from Indra to the hill, the cows and the brahmins. What near thing did you thank? Day eight hundred ninety-six.

Indra is furious. The king of the gods has been passed over by a village of cowherds, on the advice of a child. So he calls up the clouds that are kept, the text says, for the end of the world, and sends them over Vraja. The sky goes black. Rain comes down in torrents, with hail, lightning and a wind that knocks over everything standing. The fields flood. The cows shiver, and shield their calves with their bodies. The cowherds, soaked and terrified, gather around the boy who started all this. Krishna, protect us.
screen: `INDRA IS FURIOUS.` → `THE CLOUDS OF THE WORLD'S END.` → `"KRISHNA, PROTECT US."`

segments.voice: Krishna looks at the storm and understands it. This is Indra's pride, he thinks, and the people who depend on me are in danger because of it. So he walks to the hill, Govardhan, and lifts it. With one hand. The Bhagavata's picture is wonderfully small: he holds it up as easily as a child holds up a mushroom. Then he calls out to everyone: come under. Bring your cows, your carts, your families, everything. Don't be afraid it will fall. And the whole village comes in under the hill, out of the rain, into the dry. He holds it up for seven days, the text says, without moving from the spot, not hungry, not thirsty, while the cowherds look up at him. Outside, Indra pours down everything he has. Under the hill, nothing reaches them. At last Indra is astonished, and his pride gives way. He calls the clouds back. The sky clears, the sun comes out, and Krishna tells everyone to go home, and sets the hill back exactly where it was. The village crowds around him, embracing him, his mother among them. Now look back at this week. A mother looks into a mouth and sees everything, and is given the grace to forget. A serpent is subdued with a dance and sent away safe. A village asks why, and turns to the hill that shelters it. And then that hill becomes a roof. The hill they fed holds off the storm when the sky falls.
screen: `INDRA'S PRIDE.` · `LIFTED LIKE A MUSHROOM.` · `"COME UNDER, ALL OF YOU."` · then, large: `THE HILL BECOMES A ROOF.`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your back be tall and easy. Bring to mind a time something sheltered you when everything outside was coming down: a person, a home, a friendship, a faith, a quiet room. Picture yourself under it, out of the rain. Breathe in that dry, safe air. Then, if it comes, let a second picture arrive: someone who might need to come in under your roof this week. Hold them there with you. If you pray, you can hold them in prayer. The bell holds the time.
Govardhan lifted. A boy raises the hill on one hand, and a whole village and its cows shelter beneath it while the storm rages.
Your line: Govardhan lifted. Today, make a little room under your roof for someone caught in a storm, even just a call or a seat at your table. Day eight hundred ninety-six.

howItsDone: Krishna as Giridhari, the one who holds up the hill, is a familiar name and image in Hindu devotion, and on Govardhan Puja some communities build a small hill of food and offer it in memory of this story.

original.note: Sanskrit: Govardhana, the hill near Vraja that Krishna lifted.

trapdoor: what you thought: a show of strength against a jealous god.
what it means: the hill they chose to honor becomes the roof that shelters them from the storm.
what a scholar hears: the text's own image is small and playful: he holds the hill up the way a child holds a mushroom.
